content.user_title: Harden Interfaces for Real-World Edge Cases
content.value_statement: Production interfaces often fail when data, language, networks, or users behave unexpectedly. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical UI hardening checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides testing with long text, empty states, special characters, RTL text, and large datasets.
Provides CSS patterns for truncation, wrapping, flex and grid overflow, logical properties, and reduced motion.
Recommends Intl APIs and i18n libraries for dates, currency, and pluralization.
Outlines error handling for network failures, validation errors, API statuses, permissions, and retries.
Lists manual and automated testing strategies for accessibility, browser support, offline behavior, and visual regression.
limitations: It is advisory guidance and does not run tests or inspect project code by itself.
Examples are generic and must be adapted to each application stack.
It does not replace a complete accessibility, i18n, or performance testing program.
Developers still need to verify behavior in target browsers, languages, and devices.

use_cases.title: Harden a Frontend Component
use_cases.description: Review buttons, cards, forms, and lists for overflow, empty states, loading states, and error recovery.

use_cases.title: Prepare Designs for Localization
use_cases.description: Check layouts for longer translations, RTL languages, different character sets, and locale-specific formats.

use_cases.title: Build an Edge Case Test Plan
use_cases.description: Create manual and automated checks for network failures, permissions, large datasets, and accessibility behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Harden the target component for long text, empty data, loading states, error states, and keyboard access. Give specific changes to make.

prompt_templates.title: Check Localization Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface for localization risks. Focus on text expansion, RTL support, character sets, dates, numbers, currency, and pluralization.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Error Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this flow for network failures, API errors, validation errors, permission states, retries, and preserved user input.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Hardening Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized hardening plan for this feature. Include UI fixes, accessibility checks, i18n checks, performance risks, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Review a user profile card with long names, missing avatars, and translated labels.
output: Use wrapping or truncation rules for long display names and job titles.
Add an accessible fallback state when the avatar is missing.
Avoid fixed label widths so translated text can expand.

output_examples.input: Harden a checkout form for failed payment and slow network states.
output: Preserve entered form values when payment fails.
Show a clear retry action with a specific error message.
Disable duplicate submission while the request is pending.

output_examples.input: Prepare a data table for large datasets and accessibility testing.
output: Add pagination, filtering, or virtual scrolling for large result sets.
Verify keyboard navigation and screen reader labels.
Test empty, loading, and no-results states separately.

best_practices: Test with extreme input before release, including long text, empty values, RTL text, and large item counts.
Design recovery paths for each major failure state, including network, API, validation, and permission failures.
Verify hardened behavior with manual checks, automated tests, accessibility tools, and target browser testing.
anti_patterns: Assuming English text length, fixed button widths, or perfect data in production interfaces.
Showing generic error messages without a clear cause, recovery action, or preserved user input.
Relying only on client-side validation, color, mouse input, or modern browser features.

faq.question: What does this skill harden?
faq.answer: It focuses on user interfaces, especially text overflow, i18n, errors, accessibility, performance, and edge cases.

faq.question: Does it run automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and checklists that developers can turn into manual or automated tests.

faq.question: Can it help with internationalization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers text expansion, RTL support, character sets, date formats, number formats, currency, and pluralization.

faq.question: Is this only for React projects?
faq.answer: No. Some examples use JSX, but the hardening concepts apply to most frontend stacks.

faq.question: How should Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Ask the agent to review a feature, propose fixes, and create tests for the hardening dimensions that apply.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It reminds teams to test accessibility, but it does not replace audits with assistive technologies.
